title: The Blind Spot in the Karaoke Box
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep507-508_the_blind_spot_in_the_karaoke_box.json) got the culprit and the core method right (Honma; sock stuffed with ~10-yen coins; disposed via the vending machine; shoe-fit and restroom-gender clues) -- no reversal found here, unlike some other rebuilds. What it missed: Hondou Eisuke (a real suspect during the investigation, and the actual B-plot -- his return from FBI protection, his sister/Akai Shuichi's CIA-agent identity, and his love confession to Ran are why the group was at the karaoke box at all), Arimoto's girlfriend (the alibi witness mistaken for a man kissing him -- a whole red-herring beat), the karaoke box clerk (a named-in-function witness whose testimony about Moniwa's odd request is what first raises suspicion of him), the victim's miniature camera/developed photos (a real object and the source of the 'stalker/FBI agent' misdirection), and the maracas/PET-bottle red-herring weapon hypotheses Sonoko proposes and Conan rules out on-screen. The old file also used generic `knows` edges and one merged `was_at` block instead of per-room, per-person placement, which flattens the blind-spot structure that gives the episode its title.

attrs.ruled_out_because: bottle mouth too narrow for coins, no scratch marks, and not enough time for ice to melt before inspection

clues.desc: Honma's shoes were nearly falling off when he stumbled into room #3 right after the murder, but fit tightly stretched by the time police interviewed him -- he'd added a second pair of socks to replace the one used as the weapon.

The victim's name, Tatsumi, is gender-ambiguous, yet Honma said he'd only have crossed paths with him in the corridor or the (sex-segregated) restroom -- meaning he already knew Moniwa was a man, and knew him personally.
